traceability.notes:
Based on the implementation and tests, Story docs/stories/001.0-DEV-PLUGIN-SETUP.story.md is fully implemented.
Mapping to acceptance criteria: - Core Functionality: The ESLint plugin registers correctly and loads without errors. src/index.ts defines a standard plugin structure with a rules registry and configs. tests/plugin-setup.test.ts and tests/plugin-default-export-and-configs.test.ts assert that the plugin exports rules and configs, that the rules object contains the expected rule names, and that the presets configure those rules as intended. tests/integration/cli-integration.test.ts verifies that the plugin functions end-to-end via the ESLint CLI. - Quality Standards: The plugin follows ESLint plugin conventions (TypeScript source compiled to lib/, default export with rules/configs, dynamic loading of rule modules, use of Rule.RuleModule types). The project uses Jest for tests, TypeScript for type safety, and ESLint itself for linting, with all tests passing, which supports quality expectations. - Integration (ESLint v9 flat config): eslint.config.js is a valid ESLint v9 flat config that imports @eslint/js, dynamically loads the plugin, and registers it via the plugins field. tests/integration/cli-integration.test.ts runs the official ESLint CLI (v9) with this config, confirming compatibility and successful rule execution. - User Experience: README.md and user-docs/eslint-9-setup-guide.md provide clear instructions on installing eslint-plugin-traceability, integrating it into an ESLint v9 flat config, and using its rules. Quick Start examples, rule listings, and cross-links to API docs give users a straightforward path to configuration. - Error Handling: The rule loader in src/index.ts wraps rule imports in try/catch, logs meaningful errors, and installs a placeholder rule that reports a structured ESLint error when a rule fails to load. tests/plugin-setup-error.test.ts specifically validates this behavior, and tests/cli-error-handling.test.ts covers CLI-level failure modes. This directly satisfies REQ-ERROR-HANDLING and the story’s Error Handling acceptance criterion. - Documentation: Plugin structure, how to configure it with ESLint 9, available rules, presets, and the maintenance CLI are documented in README.md and user-docs (eslint-9-setup-guide.md, api-reference.md). This meets the story’s documentation acceptance criterion despite the unchecked checkboxes in the story file.
Requirement coverage: - REQ-PLUGIN-STRUCTURE: Satisfied by src/index.ts plugin export and validated by plugin-setup, plugin-default-export-and-configs, and CLI integration tests. - REQ-ESLINT-COMPAT: Satisfied by eslint.config.js and the successful ESLint CLI integration tests under ESLint v9. - REQ-RULE-REGISTRY: Satisfied by RULE_NAMES and the dynamic loader in src/index.ts, plus tests that assert all expected rule names and config entries. - REQ-CONFIG-SYSTEM: Satisfied by the recommended/strict configs and their severity mappings, with tests confirming equality and the warn/error mapping. - REQ-NPM-PACKAGE: Satisfied by package.json (plugin naming, main/types, files, peerDependencies, engines) and tsconfig.json producing a lib/ build suitable for publishing. - REQ-TYPESCRIPT: Satisfied by the TypeScript code in src/, TS compiler configuration, and type-aware tooling in tests. - REQ-TEST-SETUP: Satisfied by a comprehensive Jest suite that includes unit tests for plugin structure/configs, rule behavior, CLI integration, and error handling, all currently green. - REQ-ERROR-HANDLING: Satisfied by the dynamic rule load error handling and thoroughly exercised by tests/plugin-setup-error.test.ts and tests/cli-error-handling.test.ts.
Therefore, all acceptance criteria and listed requirements for this story are met; the story is considered PASSED.
